title: Reading the pair separator
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string and $i,m\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $i+2\le |x|$, the bit at position $i$ is $0$, and the bit at position $i+1$ is $1$. Starting from state $0$ with the input head at $i$, unary work tape content $1^m$, work head at $m$, and empty output, after two steps the extractor is in state $3$, with the input head at $i+2$, work tape content $1^m$, work head at $m-1$, and empty output.
replaced: Let $x$ be a bit string and $i, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $i + 2 \le |x|$, $x_i = 0$ and $x_{i+1} = 1$ (positions counted from $0$). Then running $E$ for $2$ steps from $\Delta_x(0, i, m, m, \varepsilon)$ yields $\Delta_x(3, i+2, m, m-1, \varepsilon)$; here $E$ is the prefix-extraction machine (one work tape, states $\{0,1,2,3\}$) that counts the aligned data blocks $00$ and $11$ of a pair encoding $\langle a,b\rangle$ in unary on its work tape and then copies bits of $b$ to its output while moving its work head back along the counter, and $\Delta_x(q,i,m,h,o)$ denotes the configuration of $E$ on input $x$ in state $q$, with the input head on input position $i$ (counting from $0$), the work tape holding $1^m$ in cells $0,\dots,m-1$ and blanks elsewhere, the work head at $h$, and output $o$.
